findings.suggested_fix: Wait for AttackScene CREATE before completing manager setup/readiness and accepting move requests, with cancellation when the manager is destroyed. Add a browser regression that holds the Fireworm image requests, verifies moves cannot enter the headless fallback, then releases assets and performs a capture.
findings.title: Wait for the attack scene before enabling moves
findings.why_it_matters: On a cold or slow phone connection, the board accepts moves while the newly introduced image preload is still in progress. A capture during that window finds no registered presenter and silently runs the headless fallback, so the user gets no attack scene at all; registration after loading does not attach the already-running capture. Wait for AttackScene creation before declaring the game ready and enabling moves, or load the artwork before board interaction starts.
findings.validation_reason: If a legal capture occurs while the new Fireworm image preload remains pending, Phaser SceneManager.js:498-529 defers AttackScene.create and its presenter registration, but PhaserGameManager.ts:64-110 immediately wires unlocked board input and advertises readiness, so AttackDirector.ts:109-124 selects the invisible fallback; the board input caller establishes reachability, while incidence was not measured.

findings.first_evidence: src/game/animation/FirewormPresenter.ts:81 -- tween({ targets: body, scaleY: body.scaleX, y: -12, duration: 230 });
findings.suggested_fix: Capture body.scaleY immediately after setDisplaySize and use that value for the release tween rather than body.scaleX. Inspect anticipation/release/recovery frames after the change.
findings.title: Restore the body with its original Y scale
findings.why_it_matters: The dragon gets shorter when it releases instead of returning from its crouch. The body frame is 615×465 but is displayed as 290×290, so its original scaleY is about 0.624 while scaleX is about 0.472; assigning scaleX to scaleY shrinks its rendered height to about 219px and leaves it there through triumph. Retaining the original Y scale restores the intended proportions and avoids shifting the neck/body seam during release.
findings.validation_reason: For a non-reduced Fireworm attack reaching release, FirewormPresenter.ts:28,69,81 changes scaleY from the 290/465 display-size scale to scaleX=290/615, rendering the body about 219 pixels tall through recovery instead of restoring 290 pixels, as established by firewormAssets.ts:12 and Phaser Size.js:64-98; incidence was not measured.
